days.theme: Arrival — Maglev in, Nanjing Rd East to the Bund
days.why: Land 13:00, and the Maglev is the TRANSFER, not a sight to come back for — the old order drove you 34 km into Puxi, checked you in, then sent you back out to Pudong to ride a train into town. It now runs straight off the aircraft, with the ride itself as the 25-min stop and the leg out of it measured from Longyang Road. Dinner is held to 17:30 so The Bund lands at 19:34 fully lit rather than 18:15 catching only the tail of the lights coming on. Old Jazz Bar moves to day 4: you have been up since 05:30 in Yangshuo and the notes already say it slides cleanly to the Bund night, which is exactly where it now sits. Home 20:45 instead of 23:52.

Late start with the massage, then a single monotonic west-to-east line back toward the hotel — M50 belongs here on the Suzhou Creek side of Jing'an, not tacked onto the old-city day as it was. M50 is held to 10:00 — the galleries do not open before then and the chain had you there at 09:44. Jing’an Temple at 13:27 is comfortably inside its ~17:00 close.

One continuous plane-tree walk from the Wukang flatiron north to Wulumuqi Rd, then a short hop east to the Fuxing Park / Sinan cluster — the listed minutes are conservative because cafe and browsing stops expand this day naturally.

days.theme: Old city, then the Huangpu by night
days.why: Yu Garden at 09:00 opening beats the Saturday crush, the whole old-city block sits within 400 m, and People's Square is the mid-afternoon breather next to the hotel before heading back out to Shiliupu Wharf for the cruise. Two fixes. Yu Garden does not open until 09:00 and was scheduled 07:51, so breakfast moves to 08:00 and the garden is held to opening — worth being there at 09:00 anyway for the crowds, and on a Saturday it now runs to 21:50 so the old 16:30 close in the source data is obsolete. And the Huangpu NIGHT cruise was sailing at 15:28, in daylight; it is pinned to the ~19:30 Shiliupu departure. Dinner at 17:30 clears the boat, and Old Jazz Bar takes the slot after it — the bar and the wharf are both on the Bund, the band plays from ~19:00, and this is the night that was built for it. Home 22:41.

days.theme: West Bund art mile, then move to Pudong
days.why: All three West Bund museums are closed Mondays, so Sunday is the only possible slot; running south-to-north ends the day at the Long Museum (open to 21:00 on Sundays) pointing straight at the hotel move to Lujiazui. Every West Bund venue opens at 10:00 and all three are closed Mondays, so this Sunday is the only slot the trip has for them — the chain had TANK starting at 08:02 and the museum at 09:42, both shut. Breakfast moves to 09:00 and TANK is held to opening. West Bund Museum is entered 11:42, well inside its 16:00 last admission; Long Museum runs to 21:00 so it is safe as the last of the mile. The move to Pudong closes the day: check in at J Hotel 17:48, dinner in Lujiazui, and every remaining sight is then within walking distance of where you sleep.

days.theme: Pudong finale — museum, Lujiazui trio, riverfront at dusk
days.why: Pudong finale, and the only day of the trip with NO hotel at the end of it. You wake at J Hotel, leave the bags there, and the day runs to a late airport call: HU7921 departs PVG at 02:10 on 8 Sep, check-in 23:10 on the three-hour international buffer. Shanghai Museum East does not open until 10:00 and was scheduled at 08:00 — it is now pinned to opening, which still leaves the full researched three hours before the Lujiazui towers. Monday is safe here: the museum closes TUESDAYS. The towers run back-to-back on foot because they are all within the same three blocks. The Pudong promenade is held to 20:15 so the last thing you do in China is the lit skyline from the river wall, a few minutes from the bags. Collect them at J Hotel after it and drive — the run to PVG is 54 min, so leaving Lujiazui about 22:10 puts you at the terminal an hour before check-in opens.

ideas.why: Hotel admin, not a sight — slots itself between the Maglev and Nanjing Rd East on day 1.

notes: Day 6 is Monday 7 Sep: Shanghai Museum East is Wed–Mon 10:00–18:00, last entry 17:00, closed TUESDAY — so Monday is safe. Start at 10:00 and the 3 focused hours still leave the afternoon for Lujiazui.

Shanghai Museum East no longer requires an individual reservation (only groups of 20+), but the policy has changed twice — re-check the WeChat mini-programme a week out and book if timed entry is back.
West Bund Museum, Long Museum West Bund and TANK Shanghai are ALL closed Mondays. Day 5 (Sunday 6 Sep) is the only workable slot in this trip — the West Bund cannot move to day 6.

West Bund Museum closes 17:00 with last admission 16:00, so it must be entered before 16:00. TANK Shanghai is 10:00–18:00 on weekends (admission ends 17:30). Long Museum runs 10:00–21:00 Fri–Sun, so it is the safe last stop.
Yu Garden is CLOSED MONDAYS — day 4 (Saturday 5 Sep) is fine, and until 31 Oct 2026 it runs 09:00–21:50 on Sat, so the 16:30 close in the source data no longer applies. Still go at 09:00 for crowds.
City God Temple is 08:30–16:30 with no entry after 16:00 — keep it in the morning block with Yu Garden.
Jing'an Temple closes ~17:00, so day 2 must reach it by ~15:45. M50 galleries run 10:00–18:00 and most are closed Mondays — Thursday is fine.
Huangpu night cruise needs booking: Shiliupu Wharf, ~19:30–20:30 sailing, buy ahead for a Saturday.

Old Jazz Bar (Fairmont Peace Hotel) opens 18:00, the Old Jazz Band plays from ~19:00, entry ~¥418 as minimum spend, tables book out days ahead — reserve before the trip. If arrival-day fatigue wins, it slides cleanly to day 4 after the cruise (both are on the Bund).
Day 6 hard stop: bags at J Hotel, leave Lujiazui by ~19:15 to be at PVG for the 23:10 check-in on the 3-hour buffer.
